title: Athena Therapeutics - inference compliance & access controls discovery
customer_attendees: Dr. Amira Hassan (Head of Data Security)
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
summary: Discovery call to understand Athena Therapeutics' security and compliance requirements for inference. Main concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration and RBAC for teams, customer-managed KMS/HSM options, audit logging and retention, and whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated or Private best fits their regulatory posture. Agreed to share SOC2 report, network diagram, and pilot sizing; SE to produce cost and capacity estimate. Follow-up benchmark session to be scheduled.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Ellis, Priya Shah (Redwood); Lucas Moretti, Dr. Amira Hassan, Sofia Alvarez, Ravi Patel (Athena)

[00:00:03] Morgan Ellis: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Morgan here from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:00:12] Priya Shah: hey all, morning, afternoon, wherever you are. We'll keep this focused—security and the access side and a little bit of deployment options.
[00:00:22] Lucas Moretti: Great. I'll kick off — we run inference for several internal tools and a set of clinical decision support workflows. Security and auditability are table stakes for us.
[00:00:30] Dr. Amira Hassan: yeah, this is primarily about compliance, e.g., SOC2, and alignment with our internal ISO efforts. We also need to understand how SSO integrates, RBAC model, and how audit logs are retained.
[00:00:41] Morgan Ellis: Perfect — that's exactly what we wanted to cover. Quick question for scope: are you evaluating Hosted, Dedicated, or Private? Or open to recommendations?
[00:00:51] Sofia Alvarez: We started with Hosted in some POCs but our security team is pushing for customer-managed keys and stronger network isolation. So Dedicated or Private are on the table.
[00:01:03] Priya Shah: okay noted. On the KMS front, do you require HSM-backed key storage or is cloud KMS (AWS/GCP) acceptable?
[00:01:12] Dr. Amira Hassan: HSM would be preferred for production of PHI-related pipelines, but if we can demonstrate strict key op controls with AWS KMS that might be acceptable. Need to validate with compliance.
[00:01:22] Morgan Ellis: Understood. Redwood Private offers customer-managed KMS integration, we also support envelope encryption patterns and bring-your-own-key with HSM in on-prem deployments.
[00:01:34] Lucas Moretti: How mature is your SOC 2 evidence? We need Type II and a network diagram for our procurement review.
[00:01:41] Morgan Ellis: We have SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO readiness checklist — I'll share the packet after the call. Note: sometimes redwood gets transcribed as "red wood" on our docs, sorry.
[00:01:52] Priya Shah: Also, a small caveat on the transcript, sometimes the product names come out wrong, Redwood Dedicated might be listed as "Red wood Ded" in auto exports, so ignore that.
[00:02:02] Ravi Patel: procurement will need any third-party audits and a clear retention policy for logs. How long do you retain audit logs in Hosted?
[00:02:10] Priya Shah: Hosted default is 90 days for detailed request logs, with aggregated metrics longer. For Dedicated and Private, you can control retention and offload logs to your storage (S3/GCS) and we can turn on or off local retention.
[00:02:23] Dr. Amira Hassan: Do you provide immutable audit trails or just event logs? We need tamper-evidence.
[00:02:29] Priya Shah: We provide append-only logs with signing options in Private; for Hosted we can provide signed exports and long-term archives. For stringent regulatory use, Private with customer-managed storage is the recommended path.
[00:02:42] Lucas Moretti: About SSO—we're on Okta. We use SAML 2.0 with attribute-based groups. Can Redwood integrate with SAML for role mapping?
[00:02:52] Morgan Ellis: Yes, we support SAML (sometimes transcribed S A M L), and SCIM for user provisioning. You can map SAML groups to RBAC roles in the Console. Priya, do we call out any limits?
[00:03:03] Priya Shah: You can map arbitrary group claims to roles. For Dedicated/Private, you get finer control — e.g., route-level RBAC and token scoping. There's occasional nuance with nested groups in Okta; we've seen customers prefer SCIM + SAML for stability.
[00:03:18] Sofia Alvarez: And does that RBAC integrate with model pinning? We want only certain teams to call production models.
[00:03:25] Priya Shah: Yes, RBAC supports per-model and per-route permissions. You can restrict model rollout and who can create canary rules.
[00:03:33] Lucas Moretti: Good. Next, keys—if we bring our own KMS, do you ever handle plaintext keys? How does key rotation work?
[00:03:42] Priya Shah: We never persist customer-plaintext keys. With envelope encryption, we store encrypted model artifacts and use a short-lived key wrap for runtime. Key rotation is supported via KMS; we can rewrap artifacts as part of rotation. On Private with HSM, keys stay in your HSM.
[00:03:58] Dr. Amira Hassan: How about training or embeddings leakage—any data retention or caching concerns?
[00:04:05] Priya Shah: Important point — Redwood does not use customer prompts for model training. For Hosted, we offer explicit opt-out and can disable logging of prompt contents; for Dedicated and Private data is isolated and by default not used for training. We also have KV cache/prefix caching that can be configured to not persist across sessions. Sometimes transcripts call that "K V cache" or "K V Kache" but it's the same thing.
[00:04:29] Morgan Ellis: We should also discuss fallback policies: can we route to a cheaper model if capacity's constrained? Is that acceptable from a compliance perspective?
[00:04:37] Lucas Moretti: Possibly but must be auditable—we need to show which model served each request.
[00:04:42] Priya Shah: We log model version per-request and have trace IDs you can correlate into observability. In Dedicated/Private you can pin a single model and disable automatic fallbacks.
[00:04:52] Ravi Patel: SLAs—what uptime and latency SLOs do you offer for Dedicated?
[00:04:56] Priya Shah: Our Dedicated contracts come with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the exact numbers in the contract. Pilot typically runs best-effort, and we do performance calcs once we see your qps and payload sizes.
[00:05:08] Morgan Ellis: Lucas, could you share ballpark qps and typical prompt lengths so the SE can size GPUs?
[00:05:14] Lucas Moretti: For our first phase, ~150 req/s peak, payloads avg 800 tokens including context, latency target 150-200ms p95 for interactive endpoints. Batch jobs are larger but less sensitive.
[00:05:27] Priya Shah: Great, that's helpful. We'll use that to estimate batch and stream throughput. For 150 rps at 800 tokens, we probably recommend Dedicated with 2x A100-equivalent nodes for redundancy—I'll put numbers in the sizing doc.
[00:05:41] Sofia Alvarez: Any constraints about network connectivity—do you support private peering to our VPC?
[00:05:47] Priya Shah: Yes, for Dedicated we support VPC peering and private endpoints. For Private you host the control plane in your VPC and we ship an appliance for on-prem. We'll share the network diagram.
[00:05:58] Dr. Amira Hassan: For auditability, can we export detailed request logs to our SIEM? We use Splunk.
[00:06:04] Priya Shah: Absolutely—log forwarding to your Splunk/Datadog/S3 bucket is supported. We'll configure log formats to include request id, model, user id, and actions.
[00:06:13] Morgan Ellis: Quick clarifying question from procurement — any third-party subprocessor list?
[00:06:18] Morgan Ellis: We maintain a subprocessors list; I'll attach that with the security packet.
[00:06:24] Ravi Patel: Good. Are there costs for longer log retention?
[00:06:27] Priya Shah: For Hosted, yes that's an add-on. For Dedicated/Private you control storage so costs are tied to your cloud storage bills. We'll call that out in the cost comparison.
[00:06:37] Lucas Moretti: One more: do you support region restrictions/data residency? We need EU-only for some datasets.
[00:06:43] Priya Shah: Yes, we have region-aware routing and can restrict deployments to EU regions for Hosted Dedicated and Private control plane placements.
[00:06:52] Morgan Ellis: Ok, we're near the end. Recap: Priya will produce pilot sizing and a Dedicated vs Private comparison. I'll send SOC2 and network diagrams. Athena will provide qps and SSO metadata. We'll schedule a 60m technical benchmark in Jan.
[00:07:06] Dr. Amira Hassan: Sounds good. One ask: include a short doc on key lifecycle and proof of non-persistence of plaintext data for Hosted.
[00:07:13] Priya Shah: Will do — I'll add the key lifecycle illustration and an appendix on prompt-data handling.
[00:07:19] Lucas Moretti: and please include an example audit export so our compliance team can vet schemas.
[00:07:24] Morgan Ellis: Noted. Any other questions?
[00:07:27] Sofia Alvarez: No, that's it from my side.
[00:07:29] Ravi Patel: We're good.
[00:07:31] Morgan Ellis: Great thanks everyone — we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the packet and propose times for the benchmark.
[00:07:38] Lucas Moretti: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (product names, acronyms). References shared: SOC2 packet (link: /redwood/security/soc2.pdf), Private deployment overview (link: /redwood/private/overview.pdf), Pilot sizing template (link: /redwood/pilots/template.xlsx).
